To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cyclic hypoxia increases spontaneous lymph node metastases in cervical cancer.
the growth of cervical carcinoma tumors is inhibited and lymph node metastasis is enhanced by exposure to acute hypoxia.
acute hypoxia enhances spontaneous lymph node metastases in an orthotopic mouse xenograft model of human cervical carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of acute (cyclic, intermittent, or periodic) hypoxia, which occurs in solid tumors as a result of the periodic collapse and reopening of tumor blood vessels.
the effects of acute hypoxaemia on tumour growth and metastasis in an orthotopic mouse tumour model.
the development of novel therapeutic agents that can selectively target hypoxic tumor cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of hypoxia on tumor progression is complex and may be dependent on the type of tumor, the type of hypoxic condition (acute, chronic, etc.), and the type and duration of hypoxic treatment.
acute hypoxia does not enhance metastasis in the orthotopic cervical carcinoma model.
acute hypoxia enhances spontaneous lymph node metastases in an orthotopic murine model of human cervical carcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypoxia is a key player in the development of metastasis in cervical cancer.
acute hypoxia may enhance spontaneous lymph node metastases in cervical carcinoma, which may be a consequence of the increased number of hypoxia-induced lymph node metastases.
the acute hypoxic environment may promote lymph node metastasis by enhancing tumor cell invasion and/or migration.

cyclic hypoxia may be a double-edged sword.
